Answer: B
Reason: The radiograph demonstrates volume loss in the right hemithorax with a mediastinal shift to the right and an abnormal vascular contour ("kinked" vessel) in the right cardiophrenic angle, which are characteristic signs of right upper lobe pulmonary hypoplasia or agenesis. Options suggesting leftward shift, hyperinflation, or normal findings contradict the visible ipsilateral mediastinal displacement and reduced right lung volume.
